![What's new in Hamstr 0.7.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mailo037/Hamstr/v0.7.0/docs/images/releases/v0.7.0.png)

Hamstr 0.7.0 comes to the desktop and lets your Hamstr apps send links to each other, like AirDrop.

- **Send to a device.** See a video on your computer and want it on your phone? "Send" in the + sheet, "Send to a device" in the share sheet and in a download's menu list the Hamstr apps nearby. Tap one and the link is on its way.
- Devices find each other by themselves on the same Wi-Fi; phones also find each other over Bluetooth, without a shared network. The desktop app uses Wi-Fi for now.
- The first link from a device asks: Always allow, Just this once or Decline. Links from a trusted device go straight into the stash with a short notice.
- A link for a device that is away waits and goes out as soon as that device shows up again.
- Every message is signed with the sending device's own key, so no one on the network can pass for one of your devices.
- Settings › Devices: whether others can find this Hamstr, its name, Bluetooth, and your devices with Trust and Forget.
- **Hamstr for Windows, macOS and Linux.** The same stash, settings and look, with yt-dlp, Cheek and FFmpeg built in. Ctrl+V anywhere stashes the copied link.

Fixes: text with an apostrophe or quotes no longer shows a stray backslash.

Signed APKs are available for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and all ABIs together; verify them against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The desktop installers (`.msi`, `.dmg`, `.deb`) have their own checksum files. They aren't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper warn before the first start.
